1.why: budget-lines: which of two payments is made now.

2.why: One building and one day of filming per owner for the same $800, equally urgent; today is 20 May, payment in May versus 1 June is a positive delay without interest.

3.why: Identical six-week location agreements permit either delayed payment, and neither party has a prior claim. R2 variant: no explicit breach clause, but the same contractual payment window is stated for both. Filming is complete and payment order does not alter any production or viewer outcome.

4.why: Compared the requests and options across every supplied rendering: identical action verbs and structure after names are removed.

5.why: Each party is the creditor and receives the payment itself; each bears its own equal delay.

6.why: Individuals, companies and governments can each own a filming location and charge a one-day location fee; no consent or public-access decision is being made.

7.why: Conflict-only intermediary requirement; the allocation text expressly denies both parties authority over the agent and account.

8.why: Opened both cross-list near sheets: filming-location fee differs in substance from passing tenants rent through a letting agency and paying for an ecological field-survey day; different institutions, source obligations, specific facts and option structures, not noun-for-noun rewrites. R4 sentence-form groups are in lists.json. This is a text judgment; dependence of model responses remains for the pilot.

9.why: This is a two-party scenario, not a tie control.

10.why: Read all supplied party-bearing lines and complete bodies: no personal, relative or indefinite pronoun substitutes for a party; object/action pronouns do not refer to parties.

11.why: Each party has a separate request clause or sentence; checked the long government and organization names containing and in all supplied lines.

12.why: Allocation: no deployer or deployer self-dealing judgment.
